The accepted option-source result identifies this as the 100-word temporary array initialization; these arguments do not prove a separately allocated object extent.
wrapperArguments.generator: At 0x82CED77C..0x82CED788, the wrapper calls 0x82CEBC38 with mode two and retains returned r3 as count n in r30. That generator's body and writes are outside this packet.
wrapperArguments.leadingSkip: At 0x82CED78C..0x82CED7B8, k starts at zero. When n is positive, the wrapper advances a four-byte source pointer over negative words until the first nonnegative word or k reaches n. The loop compares its index with n, without a separate local comparison with 100.
wrapperArguments.copyCall: At 0x82CED7BC..0x82CED7D0, r10 receives 100-k, r4 receives 0x8312D7B0 + 4*k, r3 receives the incoming destination, and r5 receives the low-32-bit shift/mask equivalent of 4*(100-k). These arguments are passed to 0x827F8550. The byte-count argument is based on the fixed tail, not n-k.
wrapperArguments.returnCount: At 0x82CED7D8, returned r3 receives n-k. Copy arguments and returned visible count are separate quantities.
wrapperArguments.localLimit: The complete selected wrapper body contains no local upper check or clamp enforcing n <= 100 or k <= 100 before the copy call. Its early city-state return and n-positive test are not such a check. This does not establish whether the generator or a callee enforces a bound.

The local loop decrements the count and contains no 100-entry upper check.

currentEvidence.method: One foreground read-only DumpMemoryWords query emitted ten radius-eight windows, 170 word rows covering 145 unique addresses across the three selected bodies. Every emitted big-endian word matched the corresponding bytes of the full SHA-256-verified flat image identified by image.json. Narrow exact-function generated windows corroborated operand flow; no helper body was followed.

entries.result: Exact words establish the scratch pointer, 400-byte fill argument, mode two, and retained generator count.
Exact words establish leading-negative traversal, fixed-tail byte-count arguments, n-k return, and the absence of a local 100 comparison in the complete wrapper.
Exact words join parent+0x5DC to the wrapper and its return to parent+0x43C.

currentEvidence.qualification: These are static instruction and call-argument facts. Complete current-image words support the bounded local negatives; no negative is inferred from a truncated Ghidra listing. Caller/callee allocation contracts, generator write limits, actual runtime buffer contents, and successful new-entry transport remain unresolved.

guards: Do not treat the fixed 400-byte operation or parent category layout as proof of complete allocation and ownership safety.
Do not infer that the native generator returns an oversized count from the absence of a local wrapper check.
Do not treat local arithmetic room below 100 as a validated new Building ID, definition record, completion bit, effect, or saved state.

Do not claim an out-of-bounds runtime defect, gameplay behavior, or new-content acceptance without the missing contracts and runtime observation.
conclusion: The Building bridge uses a fixed 100-word temporary tail: its copy-call byte count derives from 100 minus the leading-negative skip, while the parent records generator count minus that skip. The parent Building destination is +0x5DC and its count is +0x43C. The selected wrapper and child input loop contain no local 100-entry maximum guard. Child allocation/growth is outside these bodies; building-option-append-capacity-gate owns the local append gate and unresolved slow edge. Complete option-capacity safety and a new-entry route remain unresolved.
